evidence.raw_text_excerpt: Day 1 Convective Outlook, NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK, 0655 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026 (ACUS01 KWNS 111257), valid 111300Z - 121200Z. THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM PARTS OF EASTERN ILLINOIS INTO INDIANA, WESTERN/CENTRAL KENTUCKY, AND MIDDLE TENNESSEE. Thunderstorms capable of producing isolated hail, damaging winds, and perhaps a tornado may occur this afternoon and evening across parts of eastern Illinois into Indiana, western/central Kentucky, and middle Tennessee. Surface-based thunderstorms expected to initially develop over eastern IL by 18-21Z. Weak but potentially sufficient MLCAPE and 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear should support updraft organization; a mix of clusters and marginal supercells expected. Main uncertainty and likely limiting factor: shallow/limited low-level moisture ahead of the front, dewpoints generally in the 30s to mid 40s. Modestly enhanced low-level shear may also support a tornado risk, especially if a supercell can develop and be sustained.

conflicts.description: No real property, owner, or matched counterpart estimate is attached; correlation cannot begin. By design in a public demo.

Hail size numbers disagree between forecast and observed values: SPC Mesoscale Discussion 2449 gives a most probable peak of 1.00-1.75 inches, the SPC 2000Z outlook gives scattered severe hail around 1-1.5 inches, the Watch 704 graphic gives hail up to ping-pong size (1.5 inches), while the observed/reported values in the package are 1.0 inch from trained spotters near Maceo, KY and 0.50 inch radar-indicated near Oldenburg, IN (plus half-inch radar-indicated statements in central Indiana). Forecast peak and observed values are not reconciled, and at build time no SPC filtered storm-reports list for the evening of Nov 11 had been published. The package does not pick a winner.

Tornado warning versus no confirmed tornado: a cell triggered a tornado warning in western Indiana and was moving south and weakening as of about 5:45 p.m. (per the IndyStar live blog quoting an NWS meteorologist), and SPC products and Watch 704 list only a low/possible tornado risk (a couple possible in the watch graphic). No tornado report appears in any SPC product fetched at build time. This package records a tornado WARNING, not a tornado, and must not be used as tornado-damage evidence.

Temporal evolution, not a contradiction: the morning SPC Day 1 outlook (0655 AM CST) was Marginal Risk and the NWS Wilmington Hazardous Weather Outlook (12:09 AM EST) said the probability for widespread hazardous weather was low with spotter activation not expected; by the 2000Z SPC update the risk was upgraded to Slight (15% hail and wind probabilities) and NWS Louisville added a Level 2 Slight risk, followed by Watch 704 and evening severe warnings. The globe view must show items with their own valid times, not one risk level for the day.

decision.rationale: PUBLIC / DEMO. LIVE same-day severe hail/wind evidence and provenance succeeded, and two hard problems were caught and held open instead of smoothed over (forecast hail peak 1.00-1.75 inches versus observed 1.0 inch at Maceo and 0.50 inch radar-indicated at Oldenburg; a tornado warning in western Indiana with no confirmed tornado). A consequential claim decision is still prohibited until a real property and owner exist, matched evidence, deterministic correlation, two-layer validation, and human approval are complete. Recommendation: approve for inspection only, if a real property in this area were ever presented by a real owner.
